title: Green's Theorem for Concrete Simply-Connected Regions (TypeI)

problemStatement.formal: \text{Replace } \texttt{GreenRegion where dummy : Unit} \text{ with a concrete TypeIRegion structure and state a non-trivial Green's theorem}
problemStatement.plain: The base GreensTheorem.lean has only a dummy placeholder with no mathematical content. Can we define a concrete simply-connected region and state a meaningful Green's theorem for it?
whyMatters: Demonstrates that Lean 4 can formalize the standard Apostol definition of vertically simple regions
Connects abstract placeholders to genuine geometric structures with proof obligations
Enables future work on full Green's theorem via FTC + chain rule for variable integration limits

proven: TypeIRegion structure: 4 real-valued fields + 2 proof obligations (no dummy : Unit)
typeI_lower_mem / typeI_upper_mem: boundary curves lie in the region
typeI_nonempty: every TypeI region contains (a, f(a))
rectToTypeI: rectangle [a,b]×[c,d] as a TypeI region
rectTypeI_set_eq: rectangle TypeI set = Icc a b ×ˢ Icc c d
open: Full proof of greens_theorem_typeI (currently axiom — requires FTC + chain rule for variable limits)
knownResults.goal: Prove greens_theorem_typeI using FTC applied to inner integral + Fubini + boundary parametrization

blockers: greens_theorem_typeI full proof: requires FTC for variable-limit integrals (∫_{f(x)}^{g(x)}), chain rule for boundary curves, Fubini for the outer integral (~200 lines)
currentState.nextAction: Prove greens_theorem_typeI: apply HasDerivAt chain rule to boundary terms, use integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt for inner FTC

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: TypeIRegion structure replaces dummy placeholder with 4 real fields + 2 proof obligations. Area formula, iterated integral, rectangle special cases all proved (13 theorems, 0 sorries). Green's theorem axiomatized with concrete non-trivial statement using deriv f and deriv g for boundary terms.
builtItems: TypeIRegion: structure with fields a, b, f, g, hab, hfg replacing GreenRegion dummy : Unit
TypeIRegion.toSet: set of points {(x,y) | a≤x≤b, f(x)≤y≤g(x)}
typeI_lower_mem, typeI_upper_mem: boundary curves in region
typeI_curve_le: f(x) ≤ g(x) on base interval
rectToTypeI: rectangle as TypeI region with constant f, g
rectTypeI_set_eq: rectangle set = Icc a b ×ˢ Icc c d
TypeIRegion.iteratedIntegral F = ∫ x, ∫ y in f(x)..g(x), F(x,y)
greens_theorem_typeI axiom with concrete boundary formula
insights: ContinuousOn MUST NOT be in TypeIRegion struct fields — causes typeclass resolution loop in Lean 4
rw [integral_const, smul_eq_mul] closes (b-a)*(d-c) = (b-a)*(d-c) via rfl — no ring needed
typeI_area_nonneg: linarith [R.hfg x hx] works directly — hx is already Set.Icc type, no uIcc conversion
unitSquareTypeI_area: use unfold + rw [typeI_rect_area] + norm_num (not linarith — nonlinear arithmetic)
Green's theorem boundary formula: Q terms involve deriv R.g and deriv R.f (chain rule for parametric curves)
Iterated integral order: TypeI is outer-x inner-y; OQ01 rectDoubleIntegral is outer-y inner-x — connected by Fubini
mathlibGaps: FTC for variable integration limits: integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt composed with chain rule for f(x) boundary
Fubini for intervalIntegral: interchange of integration order requires product measure measurability
nextSteps: Prove greens_theorem_typeI Part 1: ∬ ∂P/∂y dA = ∫_a^b [P(x,g(x)) - P(x,f(x))] dx via inner FTC
Prove greens_theorem_typeI Part 2: ∬ ∂Q/∂x dA = ∫ [Q(b,y)-Q(a,y)] dy via outer FTC + Fubini
Connect boundary decomposition: lower/upper curves + vertical sides
